summary.intent: Improve memory quality in the memory-loop pipeline by enforcing hard evidence gates on generated records, and fix two unrelated issues: a JSON parse error on LLM trailing text and slow summary command startup due to unconditional backfill.
summary.outcome: Implemented a two-layer evidence gate (provenance + session ID validation) replacing the soft LLM-prompt-only approach, added `FilteredNoEvidenceCount` stat, fixed LLM JSON trailing-text parse failure with `extractJSONObject`, removed unconditional backfill from summary command startup, and fixed a double-filter bug that silently dropped all singleton skill patch opportunities.

repo: The memory-loop generator previously enforced memory quality only via LLM prompt instructions, not code—`passesReviewDerivedGate` only covered review-derived rules, leaving repo_rule/workflow_rule/agent_instruction kinds ungated.
`improve/analyzer.go` filtered out skill opportunities with count < 2 before the generator ever saw them, making the evidence gate's singleton exception for skill patches unreachable.

The prompt exposed `SessionID` but `PatternAnalysis.AffectedSessions` used `CheckpointID`—identifier mismatch would have caused all Layer 2 session validation to fail; fixed by switching prompt to emit `CheckpointID`.
`summary_cmd.go` ran `summaryBackfillSummaries` and `summaryBackfillFacets` unconditionally on every invocation, causing 50–170s of silent LLM calls on first load.

`llmcli.Runner.Execute` already calls `ExtractJSONFromMarkdown` (strips ```json blocks) but does not strip trailing text outside code blocks—LLM responses with trailing prose caused `invalid character 'n' after top-level value`.
Personal-scope memory records auto-activate without a TUI promotion step (memoryloop.go:623), so Option 4 (show evidence count before promotion) does not protect that path.
`logicalRuleSimilarity` is defined in `memoryloop.go` and used there independently of the review gate—safe to remove `passesReviewDerivedGate` without losing it.

code.finding: Prompt instruction 'avoid one-off incidents without repeated evidence' was a suggestion to the LLM, not enforced—replaced by hard evidence gate.
Post-filter caught low confidence/strength but a high-confidence singleton sailed through; SourceSessionIDs length was never validated.
passesReviewDerivedGate enforced count>=2||strong only for review-derived rules; removed and replaced by passesEvidenceGate covering all signal types.
Skill opportunities with count < 2 were dropped before reaching the generator, making the singleton exception in the evidence gate unreachable; threshold lowered to count >= 1 for skills.
Unconditional backfill calls on every invocation caused 50-170s silent freeze; removed entirely—backfill now only on explicit user request.

workflow: When adding a hard gate that replaces an LLM-prompt-based soft filter, all existing tests for the affected function need provenance fields added or they will all fail the new gate.
Reject-by-default (return false when no signal found) is critical for evidence gates—an allow-if-unmatched fallback nullifies the gate for exactly the bad cases being targeted.
Identifier alignment (which ID type flows end-to-end) must be resolved as a prerequisite before implementing cross-reference validation, not as a nice-to-have.

friction: LLM returned trailing text after JSON despite 'Return ONLY JSON' prompt instruction, causing parse failures; required adding extractJSONObject fallback.
The rebuilt binary was needed to apply the JSON fix—user hit the same error again before rebuilding.
Double-filter bug (analyzer pre-filtering + evidence gate singleton exception) was invisible until a user noticed skill patches stopped appearing after the evidence gate was deployed.
Existing tests had no provenance fields, requiring 12 test updates across multiple test functions to add SourceSignal + matching analysis signals + valid SourceSessionIDs.
Codex identified that the original cross-reference recommendation understated implementation risk (no provenance link in data model), requiring a full doc rewrite before implementation.
open_items: repo_learning and workflow_learning signals have no count/affected-sessions fields; they are marked context-only in the prompt but could benefit from count tracking upstream if they are ever to be eligible for memory generation.
Existing low-quality memories already in memory-loop.json are not retroactively re-evaluated by the evidence gate; a backfill/re-evaluation pass or natural decay is needed.
The findSignal lookup uses normalized exact match with substring fallback—false-negative rate if the LLM significantly paraphrases the signal key is not yet measured.
Option 4 (show evidence count in TUI before promotion) was noted as still useful for transparency alongside the evidence gate but was not implemented.
The `matchedSignal.Kind` scoping (prevents skill_opportunity singleton exception from applying to non-skill_patch records) needs a dedicated test to prevent regression.
